1. # Introduction {#introduction}

     
   In this document there will be information about the rigging, animation work using a Blueprint, and animation work that was done for the Shadow puppet Unreal project. This document is not meant to be a tutorial on how to do everything to achieve a similar or the same results as Rodrigo did. Rather to give some information on the work that was done, things to know about the project, findings about the project, information for the work done, opinions, and maybe more.

2. # Findings about the project {#findings-about-the-project}

     
   Things to know about the project because Rodrigo wants to alert on certain things:  
   1. In the Unreal Engine project if the user selects a plane from the Quick add option into the project. The user won’t be able to change the pivot point of the default plane. The alternative that is recommended is using a rectangle from the modeling option that can be found in the drop down menu that includes the option named Selection Mode.  
   2. When Rodrigo tried to put the rectangle with the corresponding body part texture to use in a rectangle into the level for the Unreal Engine project. The scaling and/or the orientation might not appear correctly. Somewhere in this document you can learn more how to change the orientation of the rectangle with the specific body part texture.  
   3. For the body rigging it is not recommended the approach that Rodrigo did of using rectangles with textures parented in a way that can be more easily animated in the Outliner within the Level where the rigging and animation happens. Instead go to the opinions section to check what Rodrigo wrote. Maybe my (Rodrigo) suggested approach can possibly make it easier to animate and have things in a more organized manner.

   ## 3.1 How the puppet appears on screen {#3.1-how-the-puppet-appears-on-screen}

     
1. We get each of the textures for each of the body parts as PNG images with transparency for each part of the body.  
   1. Here are the following names for each texture that is a part of the older brother as they appear in the Unreal Engine project content browser within the folder named The\_older\_brother\_parts (Directory: All\>Content\>Older\_Brother\>The\_older\_brother\_parts) :  
      1. Arm\_1  
      2. Arm\_2  
      3. Body  
      4. Hand\_1  
      5. Hand\_2  
2. After we have each texture that corresponds to the asset into the folder named The\_older\_brother\_parts (Directory:All\>Content\>Older\_Brother\>The\_older\_brother\_parts) within the Unreal Engine Project. Then we create a texture named according to the name of the texture body part.  
   1. The following are the names of the body parts as materials to use in rectangles to create the shadow puppet (The way the naming convention works for the shadow puppet material is by taking that name of the texture as it appears within the Unreal Engine content browser project directory followed by \_Mat):  
      1. Arm\_1\_Mat  
      2. Arm\_2\_Mat  
      3. Body\_Mat  
      4. Hand\_1\_Mat  
      5. Hand\_2\_Mat  
3. After all the textures are in the corresponding material and set up correctly then prepare the materials to be in rectangles to use for the animation:  
   1. The following image shows how the materials for each shadow puppet rectangle should be set up before continuing:

      ![][image1]

   2. Here are the instructions as to how the material should be setup:  
      1. Here how are things should be set up for the materials under the details tab (if you cannot find the following settings then you need to click on the node named after the material under the material Blueprint):  
         1. (Optional step, although recommended to do so) Set the preview mesh to a plane primitive.  
         2. Material Domain set to Surface.  
         3. Blend Mode set to Translucent.  
         4. Shading Model set to Default Lit.  
         5. Two sided set to True.  
      2. The following are what should be connected between the Texture Sample node and the node named after the Material body part ending with \_Mat:  
         1. Make sure RGB is connected to Base Color.  
         2. Make sure A is connected to Opacity.  
4. After the materials have been prepared to be used in a rectangle and any necessary scaling and rotation is done, now work can be done to start parenting the objects together. Before parenting the objects make sure that they are in the correct place to resemble the shadow puppet. I am not sure where the image that I referenced is, on how the shadow puppet should look. Although this image gives a pretty good idea of what the shadow puppet of the older brother looks like (in Rodrigo’s own opinion):![][image2]. Dr David B. Smith could perhaps provide an image as to how the older brother’s shadow puppet looks like.  
   1. Here is the following order that the rectangles named after each body part material parenting should be in (Rodrigo put them in a folder named Second\_Puppet\_Test in the Outliner for the Level Rigging\_Enclosed\_Puppet\_show):  
      1. N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Hand\_1 under N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Arm\_1  
      2. N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Hand\_2 under N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Arm\_2  
      3. N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Arm\_1 and N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Arm\_2 under N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Body  
      4. N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Body under Second\_Puppet\_Test  
5. With the rectangles for each body part with the corresponding materials, the rectangles being in the correct positions, and in the correct parenting positions. Now the shadow puppet is ready to create the animation with it. I used this Youtube video to help me (Rodrigo) with the animation [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SESZIOIAQaI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SESZIOIAQaI).

# 4\. Animation Level Blueprint opinions {#4.-animation-level-blueprint-opinions}

I worked with the Level Blueprint of the level named Rigging\_Enclosed\_Puppet\_show. The reason why I (Rodrigo) think it was necessary to work on the Rigging\_Enclosed\_Puppet\_show Blueprint was to make the animation run in a loop. Here is a link to the video that helped me work on the animation Blueprint: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SESZIOIAQaI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SESZIOIAQaI).  
	

1. Here is how the Level Blueprint looks like:

   ![][image3]

   

2. Explanation of the Level Blueprint: the node named Older\_animation and other things connected to it, is currently not in use as of now in the Level named Rigging\_Enclosed\_Puppet\_show. The level sequence that is being used for the latest animation is Rigged\_older\_Bro. I think that with the Blueprint we can trigger a play by setting up some nodes and linking them together so that when we first play the Level from the Unreal Editor the animation starts and run the animation in an endless loop (unless we select to stop within the Unreal Editor, or some other factor such as but not limited to the Unreal Engine editor crashes and the Unreal Engine Editor does not work anymore). The way that I think that we get a looping effect is that when we hit play on the Unreal Editor it triggers the Event BeginPlay that triggers the Play and when the animation reaches end, a signal gets sent that goes into the delay. After the Delay receives a signal, the delay starts the delay time. After the set duration of the delay ends a signal gets sent after the delay is completed. The node link that comes out of Completed from Delay is connected into the upper left part of Play. Which causes the animation to play again. Causing the looping with the animation. After watching the animation from playing the level I (Rodrigo) noticed the animation looping is not seamless. Because when it restarts again, the shadow puppet quickly faces a different direction. More information about the animation can be found in section 5 named Opinions.

 


# 5\. Opinions {#5.-opinions}

In this section of the document I (Rodrigo) will talk about my opinions on topics related to what is mentioned in this document.

1. The following are my (Rodrigo) opinions:  
   1. For the body rigging it is not recommended the approach that Rodrigo did. Using rectangles with textures parented within the outliner of the Level named Rigging\_Enclosed\_Puppet\_show. From what I (Rodrigo) recall. I had problems with making each rectangle representing a body part that is not the main body, to move without separating itself a lot from the body part that it is parented to. Even though I recall I changed the pivot points to be in the top hole that is used to attach the shadow puppet together of each hand and arm. I still had issues with the arms and hands separating a lot from the parts that they were parented to. Instead of using the method that Rodrigo used of parenting together multiple rectangles. Maybe this method could be used instead (This method has not been tested out yet): Have 3D models of each body part including the main body, have 3D models of sticks attached to the following parts: both parts of the shadow puppet hands attached with a 3D pin to allow rotation yet not separate to much of the stick, and the main body attached without a 3D pin to the stick because no rotation is necessary, it stays on the 3D stick without rotation, within the Unreal Engine project in a specific chosen level have the arms, hands, and 3D pins have their gravity enabled. Gravity should not be enabled on the following things: the main body of the shadow puppet, the 3D stick holding the shadow puppet main body, or on the 3D sticks supporting the hands. Now you can animate the shadow puppet based on the information in this document and the YouTube video link that is in this document. Instead the only thing that should be controlled is the 3D sticks attached to each part to create a shadow puppet animation. Another reason for using 3D models instead of rectangles with materials was because of how I remembered seeing the shadow puppet on screen, if I recall correctly the shadow puppet how was been seeing could depend based if it was moving or not and from where it was being looked, and if it was rotating in certain angles (Rodrigo thinks). There might be some things that were not tested as to what are all the possible ways that the shadow puppet made of rectangles with corresponding materials and ready to use can be seen from. Maybe with 3D models that disappearing effect might not happen as much. Because the rectangles that Rodrigo used in the Unreal Engine project when viewed from certain sides seem to disappear. Also maybe parenting the 3D sticks for the hands with the 3D stick for the main body can help with arms and hands to also move along more correctly if the main body moves somewhere far.  
   2. I noticed that the animation of the shadow puppet is not seamless. Maybe by adjusting how near the ending part of the animation goes and maybe on the beginning. The looping can look more seamless. I don’t believe that much change is needed within the Level Blueprint for a more seamless animation. Maybe changing the Delay Duration can help with making the animation more seamless. Because in the animation it seems that (if need to revisit then please do so) after it has come to an end the shadow puppet stops moving for a while, then suddenly switches positions by changing the direction it is facing, and the animation starts going in a non seamless loop. With only the X and Y of the N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Body from the Rigged\_older\_Bro Level Sequence Rodrigo noticed that within the start and end from the timeline that the X and Y values are not the same. Where in the animation timeline the 0.00 time the X value is 1650.0 and the Y value is 1470.0. And by the end of the animation within the Level Sequence named Rigged\_older\_Bro in the Sequencer timeline with the time of 12.0166 the X value is 1651.0 and the Y value is 1453.0 for the N\_Front\_of\_prince\_Body.
